salesLanguage.headline: RX-70-4K-ARC: gets the signal from one place to another without moving the equipment
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when the source, display, USB device or control point is too far away for a simple local cable.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It lets the room be built around where people and displays need to be, rather than where short cables happen to reach.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Displays away from the rack, lecterns, teaching rooms, meeting rooms and point-to-point signal paths.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Start with distance and what has to travel: video only, video plus USB, audio, control or network.
talkTrack: It solves a distance problem.
Use it when the video path needs reliable point-to-point extension.
It is usually simpler than AV-over-IP when the path is one source to one display.
discoveryPrompts: How far is the source from the display or USB device?
What signals need to travel over the same path?
Is this a single fixed route or does it need to switch between many destinations?
avoidPositioningAs: Do not use an extender as a routing system when many sources and many displays need flexible switching.
marketApplications: Long-distance video, USB, control and network transport

consultant.pitch: Use this view to decide whether the project is simply a defined distance problem or whether routing, switching or networked AV is actually required.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
